EU's Kaja Kallas:
The Russians don't want anybody strong on the other side because they want to push through their maximum demands, like they have always done.
Their tactics are very clear. First, you present threats and ultimatums.
You use force, and then you just wait because there will always be people in the West who will offer you something you didn't have before. And every time, you go further.
If you negotiate with anybody, you want the other side to be as weak as possible so that you can get what you want. That's very clear.
But it's not up to them to say otherwise. If we give them that right, we are actually giving them leverage that they shouldn't have.

Pakistan’s PM Shehbaz Sharif:
The 1.7 million British citizens of Pakistani heritage are not simply a bridge between our countries. They are the living embodiment of its greatest strength.
Last year, I expressed the hope that direct flights to London would resume. I am delighted that this has now become a reality.

Germany's Merkel on Israel:
If you try to put yourself in the position of an Israeli prime minister, it is an incredibly difficult task.
If there is a bunker beneath every kindergarten and every hospital, and Hamas is sitting there, knowing that I can only destroy its position if I also attack what is above it, then the task becomes at least somewhat more complicated.
An Israeli prime minister must do everything to promise his citizens security, just as our citizens in Germany expect from those who govern them.

Pakistan’s PM Shehbaz Sharif:
I adjusted my travel plans to join our British friends this evening to celebrate the 78th birthday of His Majesty King Charles III.
His Majesty's life has been marked by an unwavering commitment to public service.

Germany's Merkel criticizes Palestinians for "not confronting" Hamas:
What surprises me is that we have heard very, very few people from the Gaza Strip critically confronting Hamas.

Pakistan’s PM Shehbaz Sharif:
The people of Pakistan have deep affection for the British royal family.
Her late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II visited Pakistan in 1961, when we were all little children, and returned in 1997, when we were grown up, to join us in celebrating the 50th anniversary of our independence.
His Majesty's own visit to Pakistan in 2006 with Her Majesty Queen Camilla remains a cherished memory.

Germany's Merkel on Israel:
If you look at how much is said about Yemen, where millions of children are starving, how much is said about Sudan, and how much is said about Israel, then there is also a certain disproportionality in having virtually no discussion about other places.

Germany's Merkel:
The claim that I believed we could take in every refugee from the entire world was never my position.
My point was that even when someone has no right to remain here, it is a human being who arrives, not refugee flows or anonymous masses.

Germany's Merkel:
Israel's right to exist is part of Germany's raison d'état.
I must always keep in mind how I can help ensure that the State of Israel continues to exist and, preferably, can also live in peace.

Germany's Merkel:
If you take Israel's right to exist seriously, and I believe we must take it seriously, then there are certain one-sided statements that I cannot understand and that I reject.
Die Linke in Berlin has a particular problem in this regard.

Biden:
I believed I was the best person to do it. I was the only person who had ever beaten Donald Trump. And I felt I was the best person to do it again.
Biden also dismisses suggestions that another Democrat would have had a better chance of defeating Trump.
I did not believe any one of them was a stronger candidate than me, or had a better chance of winning in 2024.
